passages.text: Be imitators of God, therefore, as beloved children, and walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God.
passages.sermon:
God is holy and loving.
God calls you His beloved children.
God wants you to imitate Him.
Imitate God in your actions and attitudes.
Live as dearly loved children.
Walk in love every day.
Christ loved us.
Christ gave Himself up for us.
Christ offered Himself to God for us.
His sacrifice was pleasing to God.
Follow Christ’s example of love and self-giving.
passages.original: Γίνεσθε οὖν μιμηταὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὡς τέκνα ἀγαπητά καὶ περιπατεῖτε ἐν ἀγάπῃ καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς καὶ παρέδωκεν ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν προσφορὰν καὶ θυσίαν τῷ Θεῷ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας

passages.text: But among you, as is proper among the saints, there must not be even a hint of sexual immorality, or of any kind of impurity, or of greed.
passages.sermon:
You are saints.
Saints belong to God.
You must not allow sexual immorality among you.
You must not allow any kind of impurity among you.
You must not allow greed among you.
These things are not proper for saints.
passages.original: Πορνεία δὲ καὶ ἀκαθαρσία πᾶσα ἢ πλεονεξία μηδὲ ὀνομαζέσθω ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς πρέπει ἁγίοις

passages.text: Nor should there be obscenity, foolish talk, or crude joking, which are out of character, but rather thanksgiving.
passages.sermon:
Obscenity is not proper for God’s people.
Foolish talk is not proper for God’s people.
Crude joking is not proper for God’s people.
These things do not belong among God’s people.
Instead, give thanks.
passages.original: καὶ αἰσχρότης καὶ μωρολογία ἢ εὐτραπελία ἃ οὐκ ἀνῆκεν ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εὐχαριστία

passages.text: For of this you can be sure: No immoral, impure, or greedy person (that is, an idolater), has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the saints in Ephesus.
He teaches about the kingdom of Christ and of God.
You can be sure of this truth.
No immoral person will inherit the kingdom of Christ and of God.
No impure person will inherit the kingdom of Christ and of God.
No greedy person will inherit the kingdom of Christ and of God.
A greedy person is an idolater.
An idolater has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
passages.original: τοῦτο γὰρ ἴστε γινώσκοντες ὅτι πᾶς πόρνος ἢ ἀκάθαρτος ἢ πλεονέκτης ὅ ἐστιν εἰδωλολάτρης οὐκ ἔχει κληρονομίαν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of such things the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.
passages.sermon:
Do not let anyone deceive you.
Some people use empty words.
Empty words are false and meaningless.
God becomes angry because of these things.
God’s wrath comes on the sons of disobedience.
The sons of disobedience are those who do not obey God.
passages.original: Μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς ἀπατάτω κενοῖς λόγοις διὰ ταῦτα γὰρ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς ἀπειθείας

passages.text: Therefore do not be partakers with them.
passages.sermon:
God warns believers.
Some people live in disobedience.
They do evil things.
God’s wrath comes because of these things.
Do not join them.
Do not share in their actions.
passages.original: μὴ οὖν γίνεσθε συμμέτοχοι αὐτῶν

passages.text: For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light, for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth.
passages.sermon:
You were once darkness.
You lived apart from God.
Now you are light in the Lord.
God has changed you.
Live as children of light.
Children of light do what is good.
Children of light do what is right.
Children of light speak and act with truth.
The fruit of light is goodness.
The fruit of light is righteousness.
The fruit of light is truth.
passages.original: Ἦτε γάρ ποτε σκότος νῦν δὲ φῶς ἐν Κυρίῳ ὡς τέκνα φωτὸς περιπατεῖτε ὁ γὰρ καρπὸς τοῦ φωτὸς ἐν πάσῃ ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ

passages.text: Test and prove what pleases the Lord.
passages.sermon:
You are now light in the Lord.
You must walk as children of light.
You must test what pleases the Lord.
You must prove what is acceptable to Him.
passages.original: δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστιν εὐάρεστον τῷ Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Have no fellowship with the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather expose them.
passages.sermon:
Do not join in the fruitless deeds of darkness.
Do not share in these actions.
Instead, expose these deeds.
Show them for what they are.
passages.original: Καὶ μὴ συνκοινωνεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς ἀκάρποις τοῦ σκότους μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἐλέγχετε

passages.text: For it is shameful even to mention what the disobedient do in secret.
passages.sermon: The disobedient do things in secret.\r\nThese things are shameful.\r\nIt is shameful even to mention these things.
passages.original: τὰ γὰρ κρυφῇ γινόμενα ὑπ’ αὐτῶν αἰσχρόν ἐστιν καὶ λέγειν

passages.text: But everything exposed by the light becomes visible, for everything that is illuminated becomes a light itself.
passages.sermon:
Light exposes all things.
Light makes hidden things visible.
Anything that light reveals becomes visible.
Everything that becomes visible by light becomes light itself.
passages.original: τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐλεγχόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ φωτὸς φανεροῦται πᾶν γὰρ τὸ φανερούμενον φῶς ἐστιν

passages.text: So it is said: “Wake up, O sleeper, rise up from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians in Ephesus.
He calls them to leave their old sinful ways.
He says, “Wake up, you who are sleeping.”
He says, “Rise up from the dead.”
He says, “Christ will shine on you.”
passages.original: διὸ λέγει Ἔγειρε ὁ καθεύδων καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ ἐπιφαύσει σοι ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: Pay careful attention, then, to how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christians in Ephesus.
He tells them to pay careful attention to how they live.
He commands them not to live as unwise people.
He commands them to live as wise people.
He tells them to make the best use of their time.
He explains that the days are evil.
passages.original: Βλέπετε οὖν ἀκριβῶς πῶς περιπατεῖτε μὴ ὡς ἄσοφοι ἀλλ’ ὡς σοφοί ἐξαγοραζόμενοι τὸν καιρόν ὅτι αἱ ἡμέραι πονηραί εἰσιν

passages.text: Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord’s will is.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christians in Ephesus.
He warns them.
Do not be foolish.
Instead, understand what the Lord wants.
Know the will of the Lord.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο μὴ γίνεσθε ἄφρονες ἀλλὰ συνίετε τί τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to reckless indiscretion. Instead, be filled with the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Ephesus.
He warns them about their behavior.
Do not get drunk on wine.
Drunkenness leads to reckless living.
Instead, be filled with the Holy Spirit.
passages.original: καὶ μὴ μεθύσκεσθε οἴνῳ ἐν ᾧ ἐστιν ἀσωτία ἀλλὰ πληροῦσθε ἐν Πνεύματι

passages.text: Speak to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Sing and make music in your hearts to the Lord, always giving thanks to God the Father for everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Speak to one another with psalms.
Speak to one another with hymns.
Speak to one another with spiritual songs.
Sing to the Lord in your hearts.
Make music to the Lord in your hearts.
Always give thanks to God the Father for everything.
Give thanks in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: λαλοῦντες ἑαυτοῖς ἐν ψαλμοῖς καὶ ὕμνοις καὶ ᾠδαῖς πνευματικαῖς ᾄδοντες καὶ ψάλλοντες τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ εὐχαριστοῦντες πάντοτε ὑπὲρ πάντων ἐν ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί

passages.text: Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in the church.
He tells them to submit to one another.
They must do this out of reverence for Christ.
Reverence for Christ means deep respect and honor for Him.
Each believer should show humility to others.
Each believer should put others first because they respect Christ.
passages.original: Ὑποτασσόμενοι ἀλλήλοις ἐν φόβῳ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Wives, submit to your husbands as to the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Wives, submit to your own husbands.
Submit as you would to the Lord.
The Lord is Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is the head of the church.
The husband is the head of the wife.
Submit with respect and honor.
Submit in everything, as the church submits to Christ.
passages.original: Αἱ γυναῖκες τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν ὡς τῷ Κυρίῳ

passages.text: For the husband is the head of the wife as Christ is the head of the church, His body, of which He is the Savior.
passages.sermon:
The husband is the head of the wife.
Christ is the head of the church.
The church is Christ’s body.
Christ is the Savior of the church.
passages.original: ὅτι ἀνήρ ἐστιν κεφαλὴ τῆς γυναικὸς ὡς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς κεφαλὴ τῆς ἐκκλησίας αὐτὸς σωτὴρ τοῦ σώματος

passages.text: Now as the church submits to Christ, so also wives should submit to their husbands in everything.
passages.sermon: The church submits to Christ.\r\nWives should submit to their husbands in everything, just as the church submits to Christ.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία ὑποτάσσεται τῷ Χριστῷ οὕτως καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τοῖς ἀνδράσιν ἐν παντί

passages.text: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for her to sanctify her, cleansing her by the washing with water through the word, and to present her to Himself as a glorious church, without stain or wrinkle or any such blemish, but holy and blameless.
passages.sermon:
Husbands, love your wives.
Christ loved the church.
Christ gave Himself up for the church.
Christ did this to make the church holy.
Christ cleansed the church by washing with water through the word.
Christ wanted to present the church to Himself as glorious.
The church should not have any stain.
The church should not have any wrinkle.
The church should not have any kind of blemish.
The church should be holy.
The church should be blameless.
passages.original: Οἱ ἄνδρες ἀγαπᾶτε τὰς γυναῖκας καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ἑαυτὸν παρέδωκεν ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς ἵνα αὐτὴν ἁγιάσῃ καθαρίσας τῷ λουτρῷ τοῦ ὕδατος ἐν ῥήματι ἵνα παραστήσῃ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ ἔνδοξον τὴν ἐκκλησίαν μὴ ἔχουσαν σπίλον ἢ ῥυτίδα ἤ τι τῶν τοιούτων ἀλλ’ ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ ἄμωμος

passages.text: In the same way, husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself.
passages.sermon: Husbands must love their wives.\r\nHusbands should love their wives as they love their own bodies.\r\nA man who loves his wife loves himself.
passages.original: Οὕτως ὀφείλουσιν καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες ἀγαπᾶν τὰς ἑαυτῶν γυναῖκας ὡς τὰ ἑαυτῶν σώματα ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα ἑαυτὸν ἀγαπᾷ

passages.text: Indeed, no one ever hated his own body, but he nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ does the church.
passages.sermon:
No one ever hated his own body.
Each person nourishes his own body.
Each person cherishes his own body.
Christ nourishes the church.
Christ cherishes the church.
Christ treats the church as a person treats his own body.
passages.original: οὐδεὶς γάρ ποτε τὴν ἑαυτοῦ σάρκα ἐμίσησεν ἀλλὰ ἐκτρέφει καὶ θάλπει αὐτήν καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν

passages.text: For we are members of His body.
passages.sermon: We belong to Christ.\r\nWe are members of His body.
passages.original: ὅτι μέλη ἐσμὲν τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ

passages.text: “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.”
passages.sermon:
A man will leave his father.
A man will leave his mother.
He will join with his wife.
The man and his wife will become one flesh.
passages.original: Ἀντὶ τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ προσκολληθήσεται πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν

passages.text: This mystery is profound, but I am speaking about Christ and the church.
passages.sermon:
This mystery is very great.
I am speaking about Christ.
I am speaking about the church.
Christ and the church are the subject of this mystery.
passages.original: τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο μέγα ἐστίν ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν

passages.text: Nevertheless, each one of you also must love his wife as he loves himself, and the wife must respect her husband.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christian husbands and wives.
Each husband must love his own wife.
He must love her as he loves himself.
Each wife must respect her own husband.
passages.original: πλὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς οἱ καθ’ ἕνα ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα οὕτως ἀγαπάτω ὡς ἑαυτόν ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἵνα φοβῆται τὸν ἄνδρα
